items.name: VIP (Vasoactive intestinal peptide)
items.benefits: Investigational inhaled VIP/aviptadil produced short-lived pulmonary vasodilation in a small physiological study. Disease-treatment evidence remains mixed and route-specific: a larger placebo-controlled intravenous aviptadil trial did not improve COVID-19 respiratory-failure outcomes. This does not establish benefits for intranasal wellness, chronic fatigue, or nonspecific inflammation protocols.

source_statements.excerpt: Some groups should not use VIP without close medical guidance. Because VIP can affect the pancreas, anyone with a history of pancreatitis or rising lipase should avoid it or stop.
Pregnant or breastfeeding people (safety not established).
People with active cancer should discuss first; VIP receptors are overexpressed on some tumors, which is a theoretical concern.

source_statements.subsection: Q10: Who should avoid VIP peptide?
source_statements.excerpt: People with a history of pancreatitis or elevated lipase, pregnant or breastfeeding people, people with very low blood pressure, and people with active cancer should not use VIP without close medical guidance. A clinician should review your full history first.
Be skeptical of the week-by-week 'benefit timelines' on supplier sheets. Those are marketing summaries, not trial endpoints, and they list far more conditions than the evidence supports.

Where VIP has been studied under supervision, monitoring matters more than a fixed timeline. In the clinic CIRS protocol, lipase is rechecked after the first dose, about two weeks in, and after any increase, with longer-term tracking of symptoms and labs. For most marketed VIP uses, there is still no strong trial evidence showing a predictable benefit

Intravenous Aviptadil for Critical COVID-19 With Respiratory Failure (NCT04311697).
Vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP) corrects chronic inflammatory response syndrome (CIRS) acquired following exposure to water-damaged buildings.
RNA-Seq on patients with CIRS treated with VIP shows a shift in metabolic state and innate immune functions that coincide with healing.

Anticipated pharmacological role of aviptadil (synthetic VIP): VPAC receptor mechanism and lung biology.
